page: Vultr vbm-64c-1536gb-amd is a bare metal server belonging to the Bare Metal NVMe family. It is equipped with an AMD EPYC 9354 processor featuring 64 physical cores and 128 vCPUs via two threads per core. The dedicated CPU resources operate at a base frequency of 3.2 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The system is configured with 1536.0 GB of system memory, yielding 12.0 GB of RAM per virtual core.

Local storage consists of a 480 GB NVMe SSD, providing high-speed local disk access, though the capacity is relatively small compared to the substantial memory footprint. The server includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No graphics processing units are included in this configuration, limiting its applicability for hardware-accelerated rendering or GPU-bound machine learning workloads.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this bare metal configuration offers high resource density, particularly in terms of memory capacity relative to the dedicated CPU cores. This makes it appropriate for memory-intensive enterprise workloads, large-scale database hosting, in-memory caching layers, and virtualization hypervisors that require dedicated physical hardware without virtualization overhead.
